title: Canary delta playbook — perf regression triage
body:
Purpose:
Quick reference playbook for investigating small-to-medium performance regressions surfaced by dashboards or canary runs. Focus: canary deltas and short-lived alerts (not long-term capacity planning).

Scope and assumptions:
- Target audience: SRE/serving-runtime on-call and onshift engineers, plus engineers running bisects.
- Assumes metrics and dashboards in Grafana/Tempo/Prometheus are populated for the canary group and baseline group.
- Canary is a controlled rollout (10% traffic) with identical config except new binary/model/quantization.

High-level triage flow (short):
1) Confirm signal: which metric and how big? (p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, tokens/s)
2) Scope: is it model-only, code-only, infra-only, or traffic-pattern?
3) Reproduce: synthetic runner against canary binary or deploy canary locally/cluster to reproduce under controlled shape.
4) Profile: collect perf traces, GPU metrics, and runtime logs from both canary+baseline.
5) Bisect/Compare: narrow change set or change config (model weights, quantization, batcher) to find delta.
6) Mitigate: rollback or tweak autoscale/policy until fix.
7) Postmortem: capture root cause, fix, and monitoring/alert tuning.

Immediate checks (first 10 minutes):
- Check top-line: Grafana canary vs baseline panels. Note absolute delta and percent.
- Check request-level errors: HTTP 5xx, internal 499/timeout, client throttles.
- Check GPU/host metrics: GPU util, GPU mem free, GPU encoder/decoder stalls, CPU steal, load average.
- Check batching metrics: average batch size, batch latency, batch queue length.
- Check cache metrics: KV cache hit ratio, cache misses/spill to CPU.
- Check queueing/backpressure: per-inference queue length and service time histogram.
- Check recent deploys: list canary commits/PRs, infra changes in last 4 hours.

Useful dashboard panels (order to inspect):
- Canary vs Baseline latency (p50/p95/p99) — split by route/model/version.
- Throughput tokens/s and requests/s — look for throughput drop or spike.
- Error distribution per endpoint and per model.
- Batch size distribution and batching wait time heatmap.
- GPU metrics per pod (util%, mem, sm_efficiency if available).
- Host-level CPU steal/iowait and network retransmits.
- KV cache hit rate and size evictions.
- Tail latency tracing links (Tempo) for example traces around slow requests.

Quick queries/snippets (promql-ish pseudo):
- p95 latency delta: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(req_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, job)))
- avg batch size: sum(avg_over_time(batcher_batch_size[5m])) by (pod)
- kv cache hit rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests[5m]))
- gpu mem usage: max_over_time(nvidia_gpu_memory_used_bytes[5m])
(Adapt to actual metric names in our clusters)

Reproduction checklist (replicate canary condition locally or in staging):
- Pull canary image tag and baseline image tag for side-by-side comparison.
- Use load generator with same prompt shapes and sequence length distribution as production (script: tools/loadgen/canary_compare.sh).
- Run with at least 3 reps across 3 different seeds to smooth scheduling noise.
- Capture both perf profiles and runtime traces simultaneously.

Profiling and tracing guidance:
- CPU profiles: perf top / pprof on the serving process for 60s under load. Save flamegraphs.
- GPU traces: use nsight systems or nsys capture for a short window around a slow request; collect kernel launch times and memcpy.
- Framework traces: enable torch.profiler / tf-profiler if applicable (low overhead short runs).
- KV cache and batching traces: enable detailed logging at debug level for a narrow time slice (avoid sustained debug in prod).
- Distributed traces: sample 1 in 100 traces and pull Tempo links for the slow ones.

Bisecting changes (code/model/config):
1) If suspicion is code: run git bisect between baseline and canary commits using the perf test harness (automated script: tools/bisect/perf-bisect.sh). Criteria: p95 latency > baseline * 1.15 or error-rate delta > 3x.
2) If suspicion is model: compare quantization configs, weight versions, or tokenizer changes. Run model-only isolation: swap model in baseline runtime with canary weights.
3) If suspicion is infra: replicate on same infra type (same GPU type, same AMI/container image layers) and check host-level telemetry.
4) Record the smallest diff that reproduces the delta and add a GH branch with repro steps.

Canary vs Canary (A/B) comparison checklist (what to collect side-by-side):
- p50/p95/p99 request latency and distribution (by request size).
- Successful requests per second and tokens/s.
- Percent of requests with batching of 1 (regression to small batches hurts throughput).
- Median and tail KV cache hit rate.
- GPU occupancy and kernel time ratios (computation vs memcpy).
- CPU sys/idle/steal and context switches.
- GC/allocator events (if applicable) and thrashing.
- Disk and network I/O spikes correlated to large model loads or spills.

Automatic rollback thresholds (examples we currently use):
- p95 latency increase > 20% sustained for 3 consecutive 5m windows.
- Error rate increase > 2% absolute or > 3x baseline.
- Throughput drop > 30% with no config change (indicates severe degradation).
(These are intentionally conservative — confirm with product team before changing)

Quick mitigations (first 30–60 min):
- Flip canary to baseline for affected route(s) and notify downstream teams.
- If model weight/quantization suspected, route to fallback (larger model variant or float model) for canary traffic.
- Increase batching window slightly (careful of tail latency) to recover throughput temporarily.
- Scale up a few dedicated pods to absorb load while the bisect runs.

Communication templates (Slack/incident channel):
- Short alert message: "canary-latency: p95 for model X increased 38% vs baseline at 2024-11-02T10:14Z. Reduced canary traffic and investigating. Owner: @maya. Links: grafana/panel, perf traces, PR candidates."
- Postmortem header: "Summary, Impact, Root cause, Timeline, Remediation, Follow-ups"

Evidence capture checklist for postmortem:
- Screenshots of relevant dashboards and exact query times.
- Perf profiles + flamegraphs from canary and baseline.
- Minimal repro script and command lines.
- List of commits/PRs deployed with hashes.
- A/B raw sample logs (anonymized).

Common root causes we've seen and quick hints:
- Small code change that touched batching boundary conditions -> causes regressions on small/large inputs (look at batch size distribution).
- Quantization difference introducing extra kernel ops -> compare kernel times and memcpy overhead.
- Background eviction/GC thrashes -> check allocator logs and host memory pressure.
- New tracing/logging change at INFO/DEBUG emitting synchronously -> look for increased sys CPU and context switches.

Notes-to-self / debugging tips:
- When in doubt, capture exact request ids (trace ids) for 3 slow requests and do step-through server-side logs.
- Preserve exact canary image tags and config; for flaky noise run the baseline+canary swap multiple times.
- Avoid long-running debug in prod; capture short windows and pull to staging for deeper profiling.
- Keep a living folder in GH with perf artifacts: /infra/perf-artifacts/canary-deltas/<date>

Appendix: quick commands (placeholders)
- Run local side-by-side load: tools/loadgen/canary_compare.sh --baseline sha1 --canary sha2 --duration 5m --shape "small:60%,medium:30%,long:10%"
- Collect nsys: nsys profile --output canary-20241102 --duration 60 --sample=cpu --capture-range=nvtx
- Perf flamegraph: perf record -F 99 -g -o perf.data -- ./serve-binary && perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded && flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg

Open questions (things to decide next sprint):
- Should canary compare run automated nightly stability jobs for top 10 models?
- Better signal for dirty cache effects (KV cache warmup visualization).
- Auto-annotate commits with perf-bench results in PRs to surface risky changes earlier.

End of playbook — add examples and concrete metric names after we standardize metric naming.
